traceability.evidence:
Implementation: - Core rule is implemented in src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts and explicitly traced to this story via JSDoc: `@story docs/stories/005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md` on the rule create function and its helpers. - The rule’s create(context) visits Program, calls sourceCode.getAllComments(), and passes every comment into processComment, which in turn uses processCommentLine and finalizePendingAnnotation to validate @story/@req/@implements annotation syntax and format (REQ-FORMAT-SPECIFICATION, REQ-SYNTAX-VALIDATION). - Story path validation (REQ-PATH-FORMAT) is implemented in validateStoryAnnotation using a regex from ResolvedAnnotationOptions.storyPattern (default defined in src/rules/helpers/valid-annotation-options.ts as `^docs/stories/[0-9]+\.[0-9]+-DEV-[\w-]+\.story\.md$`). Missing vs invalid values are distinguished and reported with buildStoryErrorMessage. - Requirement ID validation (REQ-REQ-FORMAT) is implemented in validateReqAnnotation using ResolvedAnnotationOptions.reqPattern with default `^REQ-[A-Z0-9-]+$` and buildReqErrorMessage to output detailed guidance.
Multiline & flexible parsing: - src/rules/helpers/valid-annotation-format-internal.ts defines PendingAnnotation and normalizeCommentLine, which trims lines, strips leading `*` for JSDoc, and detects @story/@req/@implements tags even when not at column 0 (REQ-FLEXIBLE-PARSING). - collapseAnnotationValue in src/rules/helpers/valid-annotation-utils.ts collapses all internal whitespace so multi-line annotation values are treated as a single token (REQ-MULTILINE-SUPPORT, REQ-FLEXIBLE-PARSING). - processComment and processCommentLine in src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts accumulate multi-line values into pending state and then dispatch to validateStoryAnnotation/validateReqAnnotation in finalizePendingAnnotation, satisfying REQ-MULTILINE-SUPPORT and REQ-SYNTAX-VALIDATION.
Error handling and specificity: - buildStoryErrorMessage and buildReqErrorMessage (src/rules/helpers/valid-annotation-utils.ts) produce detailed, specific messages that include whether the value is missing or invalid, echo the offending value where present, and show an example from configuration (REQ-ERROR-SPECIFICITY, User Experience, Error Handling). - Rule meta.messages in valid-annotation-format.ts defines messageIds invalidStoryFormat, invalidReqFormat, and invalidImplementsFormat using the shared template `"Invalid annotation format: {{details}}."` plus invalidRuleConfiguration for config errors. invalidRuleConfiguration is reported when regex options are invalid, but the rule falls back to default patterns via resolveOptions and getOptionErrors, providing graceful handling of malformed configurations.
Integration: - The plugin entry point src/index.ts includes "valid-annotation-format" in RULE_NAMES and in TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES with severity "warn", and exposes it via rules and configs.recommended/strict. This shows the format-validation rule is integrated alongside the function (require-story-annotation / require-req-annotation) and branch (require-branch-annotation) rules that detect annotations.
Tests: - tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts starts with: `* Tests for: docs/stories/005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md` and `* @story docs/stories/005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md`, explicitly tying the test suite to this story and requirement REQ-FORMAT-SPECIFICATION. - The main describe block is `describe("Valid Annotation Format Rule (Story 005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION)", () => { ... })`, and individual test names reference this story’s requirements: e.g. "[REQ-PATH-FORMAT] valid story annotation format (single-line)", "[REQ-REQ-FORMAT] valid req annotation format (single-line)", "[REQ-MULTILINE-SUPPORT] valid multi-line @story annotation value in block comment", "[REQ-FLEXIBLE-PARSING] valid JSDoc-style comment with leading stars and spacing". - The same file includes comprehensive invalid cases covering missing story paths, invalid extensions, path traversal, missing/invalid req IDs, and invalid multi-line values, as well as configuration error handling (invalid regex patterns) and behavior with custom patterns and examples. This provides thorough behavioral coverage of the format-validation logic.
Documentation: - docs/rules/valid-annotation-format.md documents this rule and starts by tagging this story and requirements: `@story docs/stories/005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md` and `@req REQ-FORMAT-SPECIFICATION`, `@req REQ-SYNTAX-VALIDATION`, `@req REQ-PATH-FORMAT`, `@req REQ-REQ-FORMAT`. - The doc describes flexible parsing, multi-line support, validated patterns, configuration options, invalid configuration behavior, and provides explicit valid/invalid annotation examples that match the story’s examples. This satisfies the documentation acceptance criterion and REQ-FORMAT-SPECIFICATION.
Test execution: - Project tests were executed via the canonical script: `npm test -- --verbose`, which runs `jest --ci --bail --verbose`. No Jest failures or diagnostics were emitted in the captured output, indicating that the Jest suite (including tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts) passes under the current setup.

Dedicated tests and documentation are present and explicitly tied to this story.
